Results.ReviewText:
I’ve owned my Ironwood 885 for about a year and a half now. Had I known that a wood fired “grill” wouldn’t even sear a protein, I never would have bought it. I’ve placed the rack in its lowest position and set the temp to 500, the highest it would go and at most I get a grey looking meat. No Maillard reaction whatsoever on any protein I cook. I even went as far as to buy GrillGrates searing plates as they said they amplify the temperature upwards of 150 degrees hotter than the actual grill temperature. Even those don’t get any hotter than 530 degrees. The only useful thing is being able to set a temperature and walk away. It has no smoke flavor whatsoever. Traeger pellets have literally 0 flavor compared to other brands such as Lumberjack, which actually helps when I use them. In conjunction with a smoke tube though, because even at 180 degrees and super smoke on, there is no smoke flavor. The closest I’ve been able to get to a Smokey flavor was by putting pellets and wood chips in a smoke tube and cooking a brisket unwrapped for 13 hours, refilling the smoke tube up to 3x during that cook. And that was just a hint of smoky flavor. 

Their marketing team is genius as they make you think this is the greatest machine there is. And at one point I believe Traeger used to be respected. But with so many other options out there now, and then seeming like they just don’t care once they get your money, I’ve decided to sell my ironwood and go back to a stick burner offset. That’s smoky flavor. I even had to go as far as buying a Weber kettle 22” AFTER I bought my ironwood because the ironwood wouldn’t grill at all. It just bakes at a really hot temp. 

These “grills” are convection ovens. Not grills. And should not be marketed as a grill. It’s quite misleading.

I ordered my first Traeger grill (Ironwood 885) directly from Traeger. It arrived about 7 days later but had some significant damage to the hopper. I have no way of knowing if it was damaged during packaging or during shipping. Without too much fuss Traeger agreed to send a replacement hopper which also included the auger assembly. The replacement hopper arrived 7 days later. There were no instructions with the replacement hopper so I had to contact support again. They emailed me instructions that were mostly accurate.

I had to contact support several more times to get a return shipping label to send the damaged hopper back.

This weekend I noticed that one of the seams on the grill cover was coming apart. Again I contacted Traeger support. Again without much fuss they promised to send a replacement cover.

Through all this my biggest complaint is they never once sent any shipment notifications. I did get a call from the freight company to arrange delivery of the grill but never received anything from Traeger on the initial grill order, replacement hopper and cover shipments. In fact their online order status on the initial order still said “Processing” even after I received the grill.

Having to contact support for hopper install instructions and return labels multiple times was aggravation I didn’t need. But they did stand behind their products.

When it was all said and done the grill is everything I hoped for.

ClientResponses.Response:
Hey Andrew thanks for taking the time to leave us a review on your Ironwood 885 we do appreciate you sharing your experience. 

The Ironwood 885 is one of our higher end models and carries most of our new technology. This grill is designed and programmed to reach up to 500 degrees, includes the super smoke mode, extra insulation as well as our Wi-Fire technology and many more as it is one of our elite grilling machines.

The Ironwood also comes with one handy feature to help ensure that nice sear on the meat. This model's grill grate comes with 2 positions a smoke position as well as a sear position. To ensure the nice grill marks on meats we recommend using the sear position which requires the grill grate to be lowered into the grill body cavity resting on the lowest back brackets and the front lip. This ensures that the radiant heat from the drip tray is maximized and leaves a nice sear for whatever you would like to cook. This is gone over further within the manual under Ironwood Features.

If your pellet sensor is not reading correctly we do recommend recalibrating it. This is to ensure that the sensor is reading the level accurately. More information can be found on our Traeger website

If these tips dont help solve the problem please dont hesitate to reach out to us at 1-800-TRAEGER 7am-11pm CST we're more than happy to take a further look with you and figure out what may be going on!

ClientResponses.Response:
Hey Brian, thanks for taking the time to review your Ironwood 885. This is not a common issue, but we can definitely help. With our grill's 3-year warranty and lifetime phone support, our team can help get you up and Traegering again.

Ignition and temperature issues can have many causes, but on a new grill, you'll first want to ensure your firepot is clean. We recommend cleaning your grill every 20 hours of cook time or after each particularly greasy cook.

After checking your firepot, check the quality of your pellets. Compromised pellets can drastically affect your ability to cook. Easy ways to tell if your pellets are good are checking for a smooth, shiny outside surface and breaking one in half to ensure it snaps instead of crumbling apart.

We have extensive troubleshooting steps for these issues in the Support section of our website, and we can be reached by phone at 1-800-TRAEGER between 6 AM and 10 PM Mountain Time. Don't hesitate to reach out, we're always happy to help the Traegerhood.

ClientResponses.Response:
Hey Steven, thanks for taking the time to review your Ironwood 885.

To get your grill connected to WiFi, you will need the most current version of our Traeger app from your device's app store, a strong 2.4 GHz WiFi connection, and the password for that WiFi connection.

If you encounter an error when connecting the grill to the app, take note of the error message you see and head over to our Support website. We have specific troubleshooting steps for each error message to help get you connected. Be sure to power cycle your grill after each failed connection attempt.

If you see flare-ups from your grill, it's important to identify if pellets or grease are the cause. A build-up of unburned pellets can start a pellet fire, and this is most commonly caused by poor pellet quality. Ensure your pellets are shiny and smooth on the outside and snap when you try to break them. Compromised pellets may look dusty on the outside, and will crumble apart instead of snapping when you try to break one. Replacing these pellets in your hopper and auger with fresh pellets will resolve this issue.

If grease is causing the flare-ups, we recommend increasing the frequency of your grill cleanings. For best results, thoroughly clean your grill after 20 hours of cook time or after each particularly greasy cook.

For assistance getting your grill connected to WiFi, or identifying and resolving the cause of any flare-ups, don't hesitate to reach out to our Support team at 1-800-TRAEGER. We're available between 6 AM and 10 PM Mountain Time, and we're always happy to help out the Traegerhood.

The wifire was a cinch to set up and I can use it to monitor cooking temp and meat temp while at work or on the golf course.  It's held up well even though it's used 2-3 times/week and for long cooks on weekends, 18 hours sometimes.  The only problem has been a worn-out fire pot which Traeger quickly replaced under warranty.  Everything else has held up well including the paint.  My only complaint is that tar/cresote will build up on the bottom edge of the grill door - you have to constantly clean this area or it will dribble down the outside of the tub and onto the ground.  Seems like a lip could be incorporated into the door to catch this residue and drain it to the inside.  I've cooked everything from pork but, brisket, ribs, roasts, tenderloins, whole chickens, fish and veggies and everything comes out perfectly cooked with a delicious BBQ flavor.  The grill will give you a very good smoke ring and poppers come out perfect.  You can get a reasonable sear on steaks although I still tend to use my egg for steaks as I like to sear directly over coals.  Overall, this will be your go-to grill and it will give you awesome tasting cooks.

ClientResponses.Response:
Hey Joseph, thanks for taking the time to review your Ironwood 650.

Defective paint is not a common issue, but we stand by our products and will replace parts found to be defective during your 3-year warranty period. Paint defects will usually show during the seasoning process or the first few cooks if present.

Cleaning your grill regularly is very important in maintaining a functioning grill. We recommend cleaning the grill after every 2-3 cooks, at least every 20 hours of cook. However, you may need to clean it out more often when cooking greasier foods or after a long cook. Not keeping a clean grill can lead to grease pooling in the drip tray or grease trough and grease fires can result from this, which can damage your grill's paint due to the extreme heat. You can find a full guide to grill maintenance on our Support page.

Grill fires will rarely lead to an unusable grill. If you experience paint defects or a grill fire, please reach out to us by phone at 1-800-TRAEGER or via live chat on our website so we can help get you up and Traegering again ASAP.

Results.ReviewText:
Writing this review after 6 months of use…. I will simply say that I regret spending so much money on this smoker. It does everything as advertised, and is very easy to use, but before you buy it you need to know that you cannot cook at the 500 degree setting as advertised. Do yourself a favor and Google search the number of complaints about paint chipping on these models.

In my 6 months, I have only taken it above 400 degrees twice (the initial recommended burn in and for one cook). After the second time, it caused the paint to bubble, chip, and peel. I contacted customer support because the metal is now exposed, which could eventually lead to rust or worse a hole, but I was told that it was my fault the paint chipped away. They said my pictures appear to have too much grease build up, assumed I had a fire in the pit, and therefore they would not replace the unit because paint isn’t covered under warranty… I’ll let you judge for yourselves about the amount of grease build up in the photos I’ve posted.

In conclusion, I absolutely love the ease of use with this smoker, but I wish I had purchased a competitor smoker for $500 and not had the regret of investing so much money in this unit. I thought I would pay a lot up front and buy a smoker that would last for several years, but now I have to live with doubt that my investment will hold up. So before making this purchase, do your homework and know that customer service will not stand by paint defects.

ClientResponses.Response:
Hey Brian,
Thanks for your review and rating of Ironwood 885. The two kinds of smoke that  grills produce are thin blue and thick white. Thick white smoke does not taste good and adds a bitter flavor to food. We have specifically designed all our grills including your grill to produce thin blue smoke, through rigorous testing, and we have found it tastes the best.

 Smoking temps between 165F-225F using Traeger pellets with a blend of hickory for longer cooks  will produce more smoke flavor. If you are hitting temps and burning pellets at these temps, you are creating smoke, although it just might not be a large visible plume. Our grills produce a superior thin blue smoke that provides a cleaner, smoker flavor.

Traeger WiFire grills will only connect to 2.4GHz networks like most smart home devices as that provides a stronger connection over greater distances than the faster 5GHz band. The Wi-Fi module on the grill will not be able to even "see" 5GHz networks. To ensure a smooth initial pairing with your grill make sure that your phone is connected to a 2.4GHz network. For the initial pairing process your phone must be on the same network you intend your grill to be on, and 5GHz networks will not be noticed.

We recommend moving your grill as close as possible to your router for great connection and urge you to check the support section from our website on WiFire troubleshooting or give us a call at 1-800-TRAEGER. We are constantly getting updates and hope that you will continue to work with us as we want you to enjoy your ironwood 885 at its fullest potential.
